instruction:
Schema: purchases(id, vendor_id, amount) and vendors(id, name)
Join purchases and vendors returning all child rows with parent name
output: SELECT c.*, p.name FROM purchases c JOIN vendors p ON c.vendor_id = p.id;

instruction:
Schema: purchases(id, vendor_id, amount) and vendors(id, name)
Left join purchases to vendors keeping all purchases rows
output: SELECT c.*, p.name FROM purchases c LEFT JOIN vendors p ON c.vendor_id = p.id;

instruction:
Schema: purchases(id, vendor_id, amount) and vendors(id, name)
Right join purchases to vendors keeping all vendors rows
output: SELECT c.*, p.name FROM purchases c RIGHT JOIN vendors p ON c.vendor_id = p.id;

instruction:
Schema: purchases(id, vendor_id, amount) and vendors(id, name)
Count purchases records per name
output: SELECT p.name, COUNT(c.id) FROM vendors p LEFT JOIN purchases c ON p.id = c.vendor_id GROUP BY p.name;

instruction:
Schema: purchases(id, vendor_id, amount) and vendors(id, name)
Sum amount per name
output: SELECT p.name, SUM(c.amount) FROM vendors p JOIN purchases c ON p.id = c.vendor_id GROUP BY p.name;

instruction:
Schema: purchases(id, vendor_id, amount) and vendors(id, name)
vendors rows that have no matching purchases
output: SELECT p.name FROM vendors p LEFT JOIN purchases c ON p.id = c.vendor_id WHERE c.id IS NULL;

instruction:
Schema: purchases(id, vendor_id, amount) and vendors(id, name)
Full outer join purchases and vendors
output: SELECT * FROM purchases c FULL OUTER JOIN vendors p ON c.vendor_id = p.id;

instruction:
Schema: purchases(id, vendor_id, amount) and vendors(id, name)
Cross join purchases and vendors
output: SELECT * FROM purchases CROSS JOIN vendors;

instruction:
Schema: purchases(id, vendor_id, amount) and vendors(id, name)
Join and filter purchases rows where amount > 100
output: SELECT c.*, p.name FROM purchases c JOIN vendors p ON c.vendor_id = p.id WHERE c.amount > 100;

instruction:
Schema: purchases(id, vendor_id, amount) and vendors(id, name)
Average amount per name for name having more than 3 children
output: SELECT p.name, AVG(c.amount) FROM vendors p JOIN purchases c ON p.id = c.vendor_id GROUP BY p.name HAVING COUNT(c.id) > 3;

instruction:
Schema: purchases(id, vendor_id, amount) and vendors(id, name)
Max amount per name
output: SELECT p.name, MAX(c.amount) FROM vendors p JOIN purchases c ON p.id = c.vendor_id GROUP BY p.name;

instruction:
Schema: purchases(id, vendor_id, amount) and vendors(id, name)
Rows joining a city starting with 'N' in name
output: SELECT c.*, p.name FROM purchases c JOIN vendors p ON c.vendor_id = p.id WHERE p.name LIKE 'N%';

instruction:
Schema: purchases(id, vendor_id, amount) and vendors(id, name)
Join with alias and order by amount desc
output: SELECT c.id, p.name AS detail, c.amount FROM purchases c JOIN vendors p ON c.vendor_id = p.id ORDER BY c.amount DESC;

instruction:
Schema: purchases(id, vendor_id, amount) and vendors(id, name)
Left join showing nulls for name when unmatched
output: SELECT c.*, p.name FROM purchases c LEFT JOIN vendors p ON c.vendor_id = p.id;

instruction:
Schema: purchases(id, vendor_id, amount) and vendors(id, name)
Grouped join returning count and sum together
output: SELECT p.name, COUNT(c.id) AS cnt, SUM(COALESCE(c.amount,0)) AS tot FROM vendors p LEFT JOIN purchases c ON p.id = c.vendor_id GROUP BY p.name;
